newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends mostly higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends mostly higher in thin trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended mostly higher in thin, lackluster trade Monday, industry sources said.
Many players were said to be absent to attend industry functions around the country this week, the souces said.
The limited participants and a lack of action in the natural gas futures markets left the electricity futures with small volume and a relative lack of direction, the sources said.
NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas futures settled down 1.8 cents at $2.224 per million British thermal units.
June NYMEX COB futures ended up 47 cents at $16.57 per MWh after trade in a range of $16.50-16.70, while July COB closed up 43 cents at $17.92 after trade in a range of $17.70-18.05 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds finished between 30 cents lower and 30 cents higher.
June PV futures finished up 27 cents at $22.37 after trade at $21.90-22.50, while July PV futures closed up four cents at $25.08 from trade in a range of $24.75-25.25 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds settled from 20 cents lower to 20 cents higher.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 349 COB and 406 PV contracts traded.
The Bonneville Power Administration said Monday any increase in capacity on the Pacific Intertie power transmission lines has been put on hold until at least mid-week.

The board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council approved Friday raising the Intertie rating to 7,200 megawatts (MW) from 6,250 MW, but the increase was contingent on a transfer capability study, a BPA spokeswoman said.
Capacity on the Intertie system has been limited since last summer when two regional power blackouts raised concerns about its reliability.
Also, several generating units including a 750 MW unit at Four Corners and an 875 MW unit at the Intermountain plant returned to service after being shut for repairs or maintenance.

The western half of the country would generally be warm and dry for the next several days with the exception of the mountainous region in the Southwest where there is chance of scattered thunderstorms.

In the Northwest, temperatures in cities like Portland and Seatttle are expected to hit the mid-70s to mid-80s F. In the Southwest, readings along the coast are projected to run in the 70s-80s, while those in the interior desert area would likely hit the 100s.
